pr.title: fix: prevent ASI hazard in prefer-template autofix
pr.description: Fixes prefer-template's autofix so that when the string-concatenation expression being converted to a template literal is at the start of an expression statement and the preceding statement has no semicolon, a semicolon is inserted first. Without it, the leading backtick of the new template literal could continue the previous statement as a tagged template call instead of starting a new statement.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/lib/rules/prefer-template.js b/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
index 99e652ef2326..0d4aa69fa44e 100644
--- a/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
+++ b/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
@@ -299,9 +299,15 @@ module.exports = {
 				return null;
 			}
 
+			const prefix =
+				astUtils.isStartOfExpressionStatement(topBinaryExpr) &&
+				astUtils.needsPrecedingSemicolon(sourceCode, topBinaryExpr)
+					? ";"
+					: "";
+
 			return fixer.replaceText(
 				topBinaryExpr,
-				getTemplateLiteral(topBinaryExpr, null, null),
+				`${prefix}${getTemplateLiteral(topBinaryExpr, null, null)}`,
 			);
 		}
 
diff --git a/tests/lib/rules/prefer-template.js b/tests/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
index ef7ff200c552..156092aa41df 100644
--- a/tests/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
+++ b/tests/lib/rules/prefer-template.js
@@ -419,5 +419,54 @@ ruleTester.run("prefer-template", rule, {
 			output: `\`${"\\".repeat(1_000_000)}\${  test}\``,
 			errors,
 		},
+
+		// preceding semicolon needed
+		{
+			code: "foo\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "foo\n;`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "foo()\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "foo()\n;`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "foo[0]\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "foo[0]\n;`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "`template`\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "`template`\n;`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "'qux'\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "'qux'\n;`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+
+		// preceding semicolon not needed
+		{
+			code: "foo;\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "foo;\n`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "if (foo) {}\n'bar' + baz",
+			output: "if (foo) {}\n`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "'bar' + baz",
+			output: "`bar${  baz}`",
+			errors,
+		},
+		{
+			code: "foo\nconsole.log('bar' + baz)", // not at the start of an expression statement
+			output: "foo\nconsole.log(`bar${  baz}`)",
+			errors,
+		},
 	],
 });

testCase.title: Autofixing a var declaration to a block-scoped declaration preserves the hoisting behavior expected by a function declared earlier in the same scope
testCase.preconditions: A JavaScript project is linted with ESLint using the core rule that flags `var` declarations in favor of block-scoped declarations, with the autofix option enabled and ECMAScript module source type configured.
steps: Create a script containing a function `wrap` that declares a nested function `foo` which logs a variable `a`, calls `foo()` on the line before `var a = 1;`, and then invokes `wrap()` at the top level.
Run the linter with the autofix option against the file.
Execute the resulting (autofixed) file with Node.js.
testCase.expectedResult: The script runs to completion and prints `undefined` to the console; no exception is thrown, matching the original hoisting behavior of the `var` declaration before it was rewritten.

provenance.note: Issue #21193 ('no-var autofix produces ReferenceError when a hoisted function reads the variable before its declaration') was opened 2026-08-06, reproduced and confirmed by a core contributor (DMartens: 'I am able to reproduce this'), labelled bug/accepted, and remains OPEN as of verification; the linked fix PR #21213 for that specific issue is still open/unmerged. PR #21207 merged 2026-08-11 fixes an unrelated autofix hazard in the prefer-template rule (lib/rules/prefer-template.js) and does not touch lib/rules/no-var.js or any hoisting/TDZ-related code, so the no-var autofix hazard described in #21193 is present at both the base and head revisions of PR #21207.

testCase.title: Autofixed block-scoped declarations remain accessible to a function declaration invoked indirectly before the declaration line
testCase.preconditions: Same linting setup as above: ESLint's `var`-flagging rule is enabled with autofix, targeting a module-scoped JavaScript file.
steps: Create a script defining a helper `function schedule(fn) { fn(); }`.
In the same scope, call `schedule(printCount);` on the line before `var count = 5;`, where `printCount` is a function declaration (defined later in the same scope) that logs `count`.
Run the linter with autofix enabled on the file, then execute the resulting file with Node.js.
testCase.expectedResult: The script runs without error and prints `undefined`, matching the pre-autofix hoisting semantics of `var` — the indirectly invoked function does not raise an error for accessing the variable before its initializer has run.

provenance.note: Issue #21193 ('no-var autofix produces ReferenceError when a hoisted function reads the variable before its declaration') was opened 2026-08-06, reproduced and confirmed by a core contributor (DMartens: 'I am able to reproduce this'), labelled bug/accepted, and remains OPEN as of verification; the linked fix PR #21213 for that specific issue is still open/unmerged. pr.title: Do not mangle log messages when a log formatter returns empty or tuple args
pr.description: Fixes scrapy/utils/log.py's logformatter_adapter() helper so that when a custom LogFormatter method returns an empty/falsy 'args' value or a tuple of positional args, the resulting log call is not mangled into passing the whole keyword dict as the interpolation argument. Empty args now produce a plain (level, message) call, and tuple args are spread as separate positional arguments.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/scrapy/utils/log.py b/scrapy/utils/log.py
index 7645b235ec6..ee357c03140 100644
--- a/scrapy/utils/log.py
+++ b/scrapy/utils/log.py
@@ -245,7 +245,7 @@ def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> None:
 
 def logformatter_adapter(
     logkws: LogFormatterResult,
-) -> tuple[int, str, dict[str, Any] | tuple[Any, ...]]:
+) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
     """
     Helper that takes the dictionary output from the methods in LogFormatter
     and adapts it into a tuple of positional arguments for logger.log calls.
@@ -253,10 +253,14 @@ def logformatter_adapter(
 
     level = logkws.get("level", logging.INFO)
     message = logkws.get("msg") or ""
-    # NOTE: This also handles 'args' being an empty dict, that case doesn't
-    # play well in logger.log calls
-    args = cast("dict[str, Any]", logkws) if not logkws.get("args") else logkws["args"]
-
+    args = logkws.get("args")
+    # logging interpolates the message whenever it receives any positional
+    # argument, so empty args are left out. Tuple args become one positional
+    # argument each, while a dict is a single positional argument.
+    if not args:
+        return (level, message)
+    if isinstance(args, tuple):
+        return (level, message, *args)
     return (level, message, args)
 
 
diff --git a/tests/test_utils_log.py b/tests/test_utils_log.py
index 7f530138714..42b2b95fdf6 100644
--- a/tests/test_utils_log.py
+++ b/tests/test_utils_log.py
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
 import re
 import sys
 from io import StringIO
-from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast
 
 import pytest
 from twisted.python.failure import Failure
@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@
     StreamLogger,
     TopLevelFormatter,
     failure_to_exc_info,
+    logformatter_adapter,
 )
 from scrapy.utils.test import get_crawler
 from tests.spiders import LogSpider
@@ -24,6 +25,7 @@
     from collections.abc import Generator, Mapping, MutableMapping
 
     from scrapy.crawler import Crawler
+    from scrapy.logformatter import LogFormatterResult
 
 
 class TestFailureToExcInfo:
@@ -311,3 +313,36 @@ def test_overwrite_spider_extra(
         assert log_contents["message"] == log_message
         assert self.regex_pattern.match(log_contents["spider"])
         assert log_contents["important_info"] == extra["important_info"]
+
+
+class TestLogformatterAdapter:
+    @staticmethod
+    def _log(caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture, logkws: LogFormatterResult) -> str:
+        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO):
+            logging.getLogger(__name__).log(*logformatter_adapter(logkws))
+        return caplog.records[-1].getMessage()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("args", [None, {}, ()])
+    def test_empty_args(
+        self,
+        caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
+        args: dict[str, Any] | tuple[Any, ...] | None,
+    ) -> None:
+        logkws = cast(
+            "LogFormatterResult",
+            {"level": logging.INFO, "msg": "90% done", "args": args},
+        )
+        assert self._log(caplog, logkws) == "90% done"
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        ("msg", "args"),
+        [("%(pct)d%% done", {"pct": 90}), ("%d%% done", (90,))],
+    )
+    def test_args(
+        self,
+        caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
+        msg: str,
+        args: dict[str, Any] | tuple[Any, ...],
+    ) -> None:
+        logkws: LogFormatterResult = {"level": logging.INFO, "msg": msg, "args": args}
+        assert self._log(caplog, logkws) == "90% done"

testCase.title: A sitemap-based spider resumes crawling remaining URLs after being restarted with a persisted job directory
testCase.preconditions: A spider inheriting from SitemapSpider is configured with sitemap_urls pointing at a target site's robots.txt, and the JOBDIR setting points at a persistent job directory on disk.
steps: Start the spider and let it run long enough that it discovers sitemap URLs and begins crawling them, then stop the process before the crawl finishes (e.g. service stop or Ctrl+C).
Inspect the job directory and confirm it contains a persisted request queue, a seen-requests file, and spider state.
Start the spider again, pointing at the same JOBDIR.
testCase.expectedResult: The spider resumes crawling the remaining, not-yet-visited sitemap URLs and continues scraping items, rather than opening and closing the run immediately having crawled zero pages.

provenance.note: Issue #4479 ('Sitemap spider does not resume though JOBDIR is set') was opened 2020-04-09, labelled bug, and confirmed independently by multiple reporters ('I just ran into the same problem'); a maintainer (Gallaecio, MEMBER) linked a similarly-reported case. The issue remains OPEN as of verification (no closedAt), with the most recent maintainer comment (2026, AdrianAtZyte, CONTRIBUTOR) still discussing what is required to make it resumable. PR #7936 merged 2026-08-09 only touches scrapy/utils/log.py (the log-formatter-to-logger argument adapter) and its test file, with no changes to sitemap spiders, the scheduler, JOBDIR persistence, or the dupefilter, so the resume defect described in #4479 is present at both the base and head revisions of PR #7936.

testCase.title: Restarting a sitemap-based spider with a persisted job directory does not close the spider before any pages are crawled
testCase.preconditions: The same SitemapSpider/JOBDIR setup as above, with at least one prior interrupted run having left a non-empty job directory on disk.
steps: Run the spider once, letting it begin crawling sitemap-derived pages, then interrupt it before it completes the site.
Restart the spider process using the exact same JOBDIR path.
Observe the spider's log output and crawl statistics for the new run.
testCase.expectedResult: The log shows the spider crawling additional pages beyond zero on the resumed run, and 'Closing spider (finished)' is only reported after remaining sitemap URLs have actually been requested — the run does not close immediately after opening with 0 pages crawled.

pr.title: Fix --sanitize passing through the bidi control characters U+200E, U+200F and U+061C
pr.description: Widens the --sanitize preprocessor's trigger-byte and multi-byte detection so the three Unicode Bidi_Control codepoints it previously missed (U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK, U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK, and U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK) are substituted along with the nine that were already covered, closing a gap in the Trojan-Source-style spoofing mitigation.

testCase.title: Printing a double-width character with a highlighted-line background at a very narrow terminal width does not crash
testCase.preconditions: bat is invoked with character wrapping enabled, colored output forced on, and a terminal width narrower than the display width of the widest character in the input.
steps: Prepare an input file whose only line contains a double-width character (for example a CJK character or an emoji).
Run bat against the file with `--highlight-line 1 --terminal-width 1 --wrap character --color always --paging never`.
testCase.expectedResult: bat prints the line with its highlighted background clamped to the available width and exits successfully with status code 0; it does not panic or abort with a capacity/allocation error.

metadata.feature: terminal-width-aware line wrapping and background highlighting

provenance.note: Issue #3844 ('bat panics (capacity overflow) on --terminal-width 1 wrapping a double-width char with a background') was opened 2026-07-17 with a detailed root-cause analysis pointing at InteractivePrinter::print_line in src/printer.rs, is labelled bug, and remains OPEN (state OPEN, closedAt null) as of verification with no fix merged for it. PR #3862 merged 2026-07-29 only touches src/preprocessor.rs (the --sanitize bidi-control substitution logic) and CHANGELOG.md, and does not touch src/printer.rs or src/controller.rs, so the capacity-overflow panic described in #3844 is present at both the base and head revisions of PR #3862.

pr.title: feat: #13002 Improve logging of failed download URLs by adding filename to message
pr.description: Adds the failing filename (sanitized via Url::sanitize) to the warning and RepositorySecurityException messages emitted in ComposerRepository when a package metadata file fails to download or fails signature verification, to make troubleshooting such failures easier.

testCase.title: Archiving a package preserves the original file modification timestamps in the resulting zip
testCase.preconditions: A package directory contains source files whose modification timestamps match a known release date, and Composer's archiving functionality targets that package using the zip format.
steps: Note the modification timestamp of a source file within the package (matching the intended release date).
Run Composer's archive functionality to create a zip archive of the package.
Extract the resulting zip archive into a fresh directory.
testCase.expectedResult: The extracted file's modification timestamp matches the original source file's timestamp (the release date), rather than a generic default such as 1 January 1980.

provenance.note: Issue #11342 ('ArchiveManager::archive() doesn't appear to preserve file timestamps') was opened 2023-02-20 and confirmed the same day by a contributor (stof, CONTRIBUTOR: 'Zip archives are storing the file modification time. However, the ZipArchiver implemented in Composer does not use ZipArchive::setMTimeName... This should be an easy fix though.'), with further discussion about PHP version compatibility. The issue remains OPEN (closedAt null) as of verification. PR #13006 merged 2026-07-31 only touches src/Composer/Repository/ComposerRepository.php to sanitize a filename in log/exception messages, unrelated to src/Composer/Package/Archiver/ArchiveManager.php or any zip-writing code, so the timestamp-preservation defect described in #11342 is present at both the base and head revisions of PR #13006.

testCase.title: Re-archiving the same package version multiple times yields files with consistent, source-matching modification times
testCase.preconditions: Same package/archive setup as above, with the zip format selected for archiving.
steps: Archive the package once and extract it, recording the modification timestamp of each file.

pr.title: Compare CredentialCache prefix path case-sensitively
pr.description: Changes CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix so the path portion of a URI prefix match is compared using ordinal (case-sensitive) comparison instead of case-insensitive comparison, since server paths can be case-sensitive, and additionally includes the trailing path separator in the compared span so a prefix like '/admin/' can no longer match an unrelated sibling path such as '/administrator/...'. pr.title: Optimize RFC5424 structured data parsing
pr.description: Removes a redundant outer repetition in the RFC5424 structured-data regular expression used by the syslog parser, which repeated an element that already contained a lazy wildcard. On older Ruby versions, malformed input with adjacent structured-data elements could trigger exponential backtracking in that pattern; the lazy match still spans adjacent elements after the change, and a focused timeout regression test protects the invalid-suffix case.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/lib/fluent/plugin/parser_syslog.rb b/lib/fluent/plugin/parser_syslog.rb
index acf2cbfa71..2b6fcca479 100644
--- a/lib/fluent/plugin/parser_syslog.rb
+++ b/lib/fluent/plugin/parser_syslog.rb
@@ -44,7 +44,7 @@ class SyslogParser < Parser
       RFC3164_CAPTURES = RFC3164_WITHOUT_TIME_AND_PRI_REGEXP.names.freeze
       RFC3164_PRI_REGEXP = /^<(?<pri>[0-9]{1,3})>/
 
-      RFC5424_WITHOUT_TIME_AND_PRI_REGEXP = /(?<host>[!-~]{1,255}) (?<ident>[!-~]{1,48}) (?<pid>[!-~]{1,128}) (?<msgid>[!-~]{1,32}) (?<extradata>(?:\-|(?:\[.*?(?<!\\)\])+))(?: (?<message>.+))?\z/m
+      RFC5424_WITHOUT_TIME_AND_PRI_REGEXP = /(?<host>[!-~]{1,255}) (?<ident>[!-~]{1,48}) (?<pid>[!-~]{1,128}) (?<msgid>[!-~]{1,32}) (?<extradata>(?:\-|(?:\[.*?(?<!\\)\])))(?: (?<message>.+))?\z/m
       RFC5424_CAPTURES = RFC5424_WITHOUT_TIME_AND_PRI_REGEXP.names.freeze
       RFC5424_PRI_REGEXP = /^<(?<pri>\d{1,3})>\d\d{0,2}\s/

+++ b/test/plugin/test_parser_syslog.rb
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 require_relative '../helper'
 require 'fluent/test/driver/parser'
 require 'fluent/plugin/parser'
+require 'timeout'
 
 class SyslogParserTest < ::Test::Unit::TestCase
   def setup
@@ -199,6 +200,16 @@ def test_parse_various_characters_for_tag_with_priority(param)
   end
 
   class TestRFC5424Regexp < self
+    def test_rejects_invalid_structured_data_without_excessive_backtracking
+      text = 'host ident pid msgid ' + ('[example]' * 30) + 'invalid'
+
+      match = Timeout.timeout(1) do
+        Fluent::Plugin::SyslogParser::RFC5424_WITHOUT_TIME_AND_PRI_REGEXP.match(text)
+      end
+
+      assert_nil(match)
+    end

pr.title: Avoid virtual-thread yield spin in ConcurrentBag
pr.description: Keeps the existing Thread.yield() spin behavior for platform threads in ConcurrentBag's requite()/unreserve() handoff loops, but avoids the yield spin when the returning/unreserving thread is a virtual thread, using a short parkNanos(10us) path instead. Virtual-thread detection is resolved once via a cached MethodHandle so the library can still target Java 11 while detecting virtual threads on Java 19+.

testCase.title: Creating a connection pool does not lock on the JVM-wide system properties object
testCase.preconditions: An application creates a HikariCP connection pool without an explicit pool name, relying on the library to generate one, in a JVM where other threads may concurrently read or write system properties.
steps: From a separate thread, begin a long-running operation that reads or writes a System property.
Concurrently, on the main thread, construct a new connection pool (HikariDataSource/HikariPool) without specifying a pool name.
Observe whether pool construction completes without waiting on the other thread's system-properties access.
testCase.expectedResult: Pool construction completes promptly and does not block waiting on unrelated code elsewhere in the JVM that is accessing System properties; generating the pool name does not require acquiring a lock shared with arbitrary System.getProperties() callers.

metadata.feature: connection pool initialization / pool name generation locking

provenance.note: Issue #2104 ('Synchronizing System.getProperties in generatePoolName / Number creates a deadlock-able window') was opened 2023-09-05, labelled bug and volunteer-needed, and confirmed in detail by the community (bvsvas, kialambroca describing the concrete deadlock sequence) with a project collaborator (lfbayer, COLLABORATOR) acknowledging it is a real, unresolved defect ('If someone creates a pull request with a fix for this issue, I will gladly merge it.'). The issue remains OPEN (closedAt null) as of verification. PR #2402 merged 2026-06-11 only touches src/main/java/com/zaxxer/hikari/util/ConcurrentBag.java (pool entry handoff spin/park behavior for virtual threads) and its new test file, and does not touch HikariConfig.java's generatePoolName method or its System.getProperties() synchronization, so the deadlock-prone locking described in #2104 is present at both the base and head revisions of PR #2402.

testCase.title: Concurrently starting multiple connection pools without explicit names does not risk a deadlock with unrelated system-property access
testCase.preconditions: Multiple threads in the same JVM each construct a HikariCP connection pool without an explicit name at approximately the same time that other application code accesses System properties while holding its own lock.
steps: From one thread, acquire a lock on an application-defined object and, while still holding it, read a System property.
From another thread, hold a different application-defined lock while triggering pool-name generation by creating a connection pool without an explicit name.
Run both threads concurrently under contention and wait for both to complete.
testCase.expectedResult: All pools are constructed successfully within a bounded time, with no deadlock or indefinite hang caused by pool-name generation contending for a lock on the shared system properties object.
